## Acceptance criteria

### The live failure this exists to fix — established by execution, 2026-08-10

Warwick sent a real shopping-list photograph (Telegram msg 63, update 171031156). He received
NO acknowledgement card. Larry established, read-only:

- intake fetched and DOWNLOADED it — the file is on disk at
  `C:\.fusion247\asdair\shopper-media\tg-shopper-chat-8601328832-msg-63-*.jpg`;
- `runtime.log` shows `emitted` (kind `photo`) — i.e. `onRecord`/`receiveList` RESOLVED;
- `SELECT ... WHERE telegram_message_id='63' OR telegram_update_id='171031156'` returns **ZERO rows**;
- the Telegram offset advanced to 171031156 and reads `consumed: true`;
- `asdair.shop` holds `SHOP-2026-08-10`, status **CANCELLED**, created 00:15 from a TEXT
  message (msg 58), cancelled 00:49.

Cause: `nextShopRef(date)` is `'SHOP-' + date`, so the new photo computed the ref of the dead
row. `createOrResumeShop` is `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` across BOTH unique indexes
including `(household_id, shop_ref)`, so it RESUMED the cancelled shop and wrote nothing.
`receiveList` returned normally, `persist` (runtime.js:176) ignored `matched_by`, the offset
advanced, and Telegram forgot the message permanently. A CANCELLED shop is terminal, so no
pass ever advances it — hence no card.

### Warwick's PRODUCT RULE, verbatim (2026-08-10) — this is the specification

> If a new inbound shopping list arrives and the date-derived shop ref already belongs to a
> terminal shop (`CANCELLED` or `RECONCILED`), create a FRESH shop for the new inbound list.
>
> Do NOT revive, overwrite, append into or otherwise mutate the terminal shop.
>
> The new shop needs its own durable unique identity. `SHOP-YYYY-MM-DD` is therefore not
> sufficient as the sole identity once more than one shop can legitimately occur on a date.
>
> Use the narrowest deterministic collision-safe scheme that fits the existing architecture.
> Prefer grounding the identity to the actual inbound event/source so retries of THE SAME
> Telegram message remain idempotent while a genuinely different message on the same date
> creates a new shop.

### Acceptance criteria

**AC1 — same message retried is still ONE shop.** A redelivery of the identical inbound
Telegram message creates no second shop and resolves truthfully to the existing shop /
already-consumed event. The existing `(telegram_chat_id, telegram_message_id)` unique index
is the natural instrument; do not weaken it.

**AC2 — a different message on a date whose shop is TERMINAL creates a FRESH shop.** The new
shop is in a live (non-terminal) status, carries the NEW message's `telegram_message_id`,
`telegram_update_id` and raw evidence, and the terminal row is left unmutated — status,
updated_at and every other column unchanged. Assert that, do not assume it.

**AC3 — a LIVE shop on the same date behaves exactly as it does today.** Do not redesign
multi-shop semantics. If execution proves today's live-shop behaviour is itself wrong, REPORT
it; do not fix it under this order.

**AC4 — intake never reports success when no list entered a live shop.** The vacuous-success
path is the defect: `receiveList` resolving without the inbound content reaching a live shop
must be impossible, or must raise loudly enough to hold the offset.

**AC5 — a terminal-shop collision never silently advances the Telegram offset while dropping
content.** Durable intake success must PRECEDE telling Telegram the message is consumed.
Audit the whole acknowledgement/offset ordering in `shopperIntake.js` — do NOT merely
special-case CANCELLED and leave a sibling silent-drop path standing. Report any other path
you find that can advance the offset without durable capture, whether or not you fix it.

**AC6 — the regression reproduces THIS failure.** A test in which a terminal `SHOP-2026-08-10`
already exists and a DIFFERENT inbound photo arrives on 2026-08-10. It must FAIL against the
pre-fix behaviour (absorbed and falsely successful) and PASS after, creating a distinct live
shop carrying the new inbound event. State the executed evidence of both directions.

**AC7 — the guard is mutation-proven.** Revert the terminal-state guard / fresh-identity
behaviour to date-only resume and prove a named test goes RED, then restore and prove the
source is byte-identical (sha256 before and after, both quoted). A future return to date-only
resume must fail loudly. Assert a NON-ZERO executed test count — a suite that ran nothing is
not evidence.

**AC8 — no manufactured state.** Warwick's photograph on disk is EVIDENCE and is preserved
untouched. Do not inject it into the database, do not hand-author a shop from it, do not
write to the live store at all. `live_authority: none` is not negotiable here.

- Cancelling, reviving, renaming or otherwise touching any existing shop row.
- The 11 origin-only documents, the stale Wayfinder frontier block, and every other documentation reconciliation — explicitly parked by Warwick for this window.
- Migrations. If you conclude a schema change is genuinely required, STOP and return that conclusion — do not write one.

## AMENDMENT 1 — Larry, 2026-08-10, on Keel's read-back

Keel held with `CLARIFY` and was right to. Its blocking finding is **VERIFIED BY LARRY'S OWN
EXECUTION**, not accepted on report:

- `services/asdair/pipeline/runPipeline.js:384-387` — `listDateOf()` runs
  `/^SHOP-(\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2})$/` and **THROWS** on anything else. Read at the governance head.
- `services/asdair/packet/buildExecutionPacket.js:119` and `services/asdair/handoff/buildHandoff.js:74`
  each carry their own hard-coded `^SHOP-[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}$`.
- `services/asdair/shop/shopState.js:167` is the fourth, via `isShopRef` (`shopStatus.js`).
- `services/asdair/db/006_shop_control_surface.sql:29` — `shop_ref text not null`, and the only
  related object is the unique index at line 64. **No CHECK constraint. Keel's no-migration
  conclusion is confirmed.**

**The consequence decides the option.** Under option (ii) the fresh shop would be created and
then throw on its first pipeline pass — Warwick still gets no card. That is moving the failure,
not fixing it, and Warwick's ruling was explicitly *"fix the underlying defect, not just today's
row"*. Option (iii) Keel proved impossible while `shop_ref_uniq` stands and migrations are out
of scope. So:

### Settlement 1 — option (i). The file surface is WIDENED.

Eight paths are added to `file_surface` above and are now yours: `runPipeline.js`,
`buildExecutionPacket.js`, `buildHandoff.js`, `shopStatus.js` and their four test files.
**The permitted change in each is the shop_ref pattern and whatever its own tests pin about
it — nothing else.** `listDateOf`'s capture group must keep returning the DATE PART only.
This widening is not licence to refactor anything you find there.

### Settlement 2 — C3 CONFIRMED, and thank you for catching it.

**Key the AC4 guard on DURABLE CAPTURE OF THIS MESSAGE (`matched_by`), never on the resolved
shop's liveness.** Your wedge analysis is correct and it matters more than the bug being
fixed: a redelivered message whose shop Warwick later cancelled has already been durably
captured, nothing was dropped, and raising there would hold the offset and make Telegram
redeliver the same message forever. A permanently wedged poller is a worse outage. AC4 is
hereby read as you propose, and this settlement supersedes its literal wording.

### Settlement 3 — A1 CONFIRMED.

A non-Telegram inbound (shop-cli, a pasted text with no message id) landing on a terminal date
**throws loudly**. Do not invent a counter, a timestamp suffix or any other identity. A loud
refusal on an edge path is honest; a fabricated identity is not, and a clock would break the
purity `shopState` deliberately keeps.

### Noted, no decision needed

- **C1 — the order's "344 pass" was WRONG.** Your measured 386/0 at the governance head is the
  baseline. My number came from a stale Wayfinder row; report against what you measured.
- **C2 — correct refusal.** Do not write `CONFIGURATION.md`; it is outside the surface and
  `document_impact` identifies rather than authorises. The two READMEs documenting the
  date-only convention are report-only and mine to place.
- **A2 — agreed.** Keep `matched_by`'s three existing values intact and report the collision in
  a new field.
- Your scheme `SHOP-YYYY-MM-DD-M<messageId>` is **accepted** — deterministic, readable,
  clock-free, grounded in the inbound event, and it keeps the date extractable.

### AC9 — NEW, and it is the outcome-critical one

**The fresh shop must be able to ADVANCE, not merely exist.** Prove by execution that a shop
carrying the collision ref survives every pin above: `listDateOf` returns the correct date part
for it, and the execution packet and browser handoff validators accept it. A test asserting
only that the row was created would restate the bug in a new place — the whole point of
widening the surface is that creation without advancement is not a fix.

**AC7's mutation proof now extends to the widened pins:** revert any one relaxed pattern and
prove a named test goes RED, then restore byte-identically. A future return to the strict
date-only form must fail loudly wherever it is reintroduced.

### Unchanged

Everything else in this order stands: AC1-AC3, AC5, AC6, AC8, the out-of-scope list, the
authority defaults (`live_authority: none` above all), and the git endpoint. Warwick's product
ruling is settled and is not reopened.

**You have ONE further read-back if this amendment is itself materially defective** (Warwick,
2026-08-02). Otherwise proceed — baselines are already measured, so start at the AC6
regression and prove it RED.
